title: Architecture, peinture et sculpture de la maison de ville d'Amsterdam, représentée en CIX figures en taille-douce ...
shelf_note: No tradition or collection is assigned. The leaf is an authentic 1719 French commentary on the sculpture of the Amsterdam Town Hall (plates LXXIII–LXXXIV), which matches the title and date.
structure_note: This record is an unsplit two-page opening (printed pp. 18 and 19). The OCR transcribes both pages in order and the translation says so in a meta, so nothing is lost here. If other records are spreads too, that would explain the printed_backsteps (4) and printed_repeats (2): each record carries two printed numbers and only one gets parsed. It would also explain the low with_printed_number (16 of 169) in a book that is mostly plates. structure.pages_translated is 0 while the book field says 127 and this page has an English text, so the structure count is unreliable (E2).

pages.layout: two-page opening, each page in two columns, centred PLANCHE headings, running heads across the spread, no illustrations

ocr_errors.problem: long s read as f. The translation still renders it correctly as 'it does not follow'

other.note: A raw <column-break/> tag stands twice in the English reading text: after "hardly different at all from the previous one." and after "the greatest beauties are not themselves". Unless the renderer strips it, the reader sees it.

The continuity meta "continues from previous page: description of the ornaments of the Pedestal of Mercury" names a subject the leaf does not name. The emblems (winged hat, caduceus) imply Mercury, but 'Pedestal' and 'Plate LXXII' are not on this page.

missing.english: the Chamber of the Extraordinary Aldermen
missing.why: This renders the Dutch civic office (Extraordinaris Schepenen). 'Extraordinary Aldermen' means nothing to a modern reader without a gloss.

book_verdict: The OCR and translation of this spread are clean and faithful: one long-s slip, and the notes are correct and modest. The only visible blemishes are a raw <column-break/> in the English and a continuity meta that goes beyond the page.
